facts.fact: According to a third-party product photography pricing guide (Peggy Cormary Photography), basic product shots typically cost $25 to $100 per image.
facts.quote: basic product shots typically run $25 to $100 per image

facts.fact: According to the same third-party pricing guide, styled product shots cost $100 to $300+ per image.
facts.quote: styled shots rise to $100 to $300+ per image

facts.fact: According to the same third-party pricing guide, day rates for larger product photography shoots range from $500 to $3,000+.
facts.quote: day rates can range from $500 to $3,000+

facts.fact: A 2024 third-party budget photography guide (buildgrowscale.com) states that a smartphone with at least a 12-megapixel camera, a tripod, and free editing tools is often sufficient for product photos.
facts.quote: a smartphone with at least a 12-megapixel camera, a tripod, and free editing tools are often sufficient

facts.fact: According to the same 2024 third-party budget guide, a seller can create a workable product photography setup for under $200 with the right choices.
facts.quote: a seller can create a workable setup for **under $200** with the right choices

facts.fact: BigCommerce's budget product photography guide, as cited by Adwave, recommends an aperture around f/11 to f/16.
facts.quote: A major budget photography guide recommends technical settings such as **aperture around f/11 to f/16**, **ISO 100**, and shooting in **RAW** when possible

facts.fact: Adwave states that 68% of AI-generated TV ads underperform due to inconsistent product imagery, citing 'recent data' without naming a source.
facts.quote: **68% of AI-generated TV ads underperform due to inconsistent product imagery**
